sentences.text:
Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. And 2 Others
Counsel for Applicant :- Ankit Agarval

Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Subhash Chandra Sharma,J.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant as well as learned AGA for the State and perused the material placed on record.

This anticipatory bail application (under section 438 Cr.P.C.) has been moved seeking bail in Case Crime No. 1068 of 2022, under sections 3/7 of Essential Commodities Act-1955 & Section 420 I.P.C., Police Station Sikandrabad, District Bulandshar, during the pendency of investigation.

It is submitted by learned counsel for the applicant that in this case applicant is the proprietor of rice purchasing and supplying shop and his shop is registered under the G.S.T. registration the certificate of which is on record and it was issued on 09.06.2021.
It is further submitted that 400 bags of rice were purchased by the applicant from the different firms for supply of rice and it was being transported to R.G. Enterprises, Delhi by the truck.

The vehicle met with an accident in the way and the police was called for and they booked the vehicle on the basis of suspicion that the rice Puneet vs State Of U.P. And 2 Others on 23 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/105726378/

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 1 laden in the truck belonged to P.D.S. scheme.

It is further submitted that applicant has filed all the bills regarding purchase and supply of the aforesaid rice alongwith registration certificate of G.S.T.
issued by Government of India.

During investigation nothing has been found to establish that the aforesaid quantity was brought from the shop relating to the P.D.S. scheme, therefore, no offence is made out under 3/7 Essential Commodities Act.
Since investigation is going on and the applicant is under apprehension of imminent arrest.
In case, the applicant is released on bail, he would not misuse the liberty of bail and would cooperate with the investigation.
Learned A.G.A. has opposed the prayer for anticipatory bail.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions made by learned counsel for the applicant as well as learned A.G.A., perusal of record and all the relevant papers filed by the applicant, the applicant is entitled to be released on anticipatory bail in this case for the limited period considering the exception considered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Sushila Aggarwal Vs. State (NCT of Delhi)-2020 SCC Online SC 98.

opennyai_summary.decision:

State (NCT of Delhi)-2020 SCC Online SC 98.
In the event of arrest of the applicant- Puneet, shall be released on anticipatory bail till the submission of police report, if any, under section 173 (2) Cr.P.C., on furnishing a personal bond of Rs. 25,000/- with two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Station House Officer of the police station concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall make himself available for interrogation by a police office as and when required;
(ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly, make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police office;
(iii) The applicant shall not leave India without the previous permission of the Court and if he has passport, the same shall be deposited by him before the S.S.P./S.P.
concerned.
In default of any of the conditions, the Investigating Officer is at liberty to file appropriate application for cancellation of anticipatory bail granted to the applicant.
